facts.text: The repository hosts a collection of robosuite tasks designed by community users and is intended to standardize experimental validation of simulated tasks
Using the repository requires installing robosuite first, and the clone is then installed with pip install -e .
The environments are based on robosuite and refer to the robosuite documentation for how to create an environment
The HammerPlace task is a single-arm tabletop domain in which the operator places a hammer into the cabinet and closes the cabinet
The documented task action space is OSC_POSITION (3) plus Gripper (1)
The documented HammerPlace observations are workspace images, eye-in-hand images and proprioception
The hammer_place module imports robosuite's SingleArmEnv as the base environment
HammerPlaceEnv is defined as a single-arm robosuite environment

The HammerPlaceEnv constructor takes robots, an optional controller_configs, control_freq 20, horizon 1000 and camera defaults use_camera_obs=True, use_object_obs=True, camera_names agentview, camera_heights 256 and camera_widths 256
The constructor forwards robots, controller_configs, control_freq, horizon, camera options and the rest to SingleArmEnv
_load_model builds the TableArena, the HammerObject named hammer and the CabinetObject, registers them with the ManipulationTask and stores hammer and CabinetObject in self.objects
The placement sampler draws the hammer pose from x_range [0.10, 0.18] and y_range [-0.20, -0.13] on the table during a reset that is not deterministic
The success predicate is true when the hammer is inside the drawer (1.0 > z > 0.94 and y > 0.22) and the cabinet is closed (qpos > -0.01)
The sparse reward is 0.0, or 1.0 when _check_success is true, scaled by reward_scale
HammerPlaceEnv.step maps a four-element action to action[:3] plus the gripper, calls the robosuite parent step and returns obs, reward, done and info
step replaces the parent's done with the environment's _check_success result
The custom observables include robot0_joint_pos (activated), the object pose/relative-pose sensors, robot0_contact and robot0_eef_force_norm
get_state_vector reads the observation keys robot0_gripper_qpos, robot0_eef_pos and robot0_eef_quat
The clone's demo creates the environment, calls env.reset(), reads env.action_spec and unpacks obs, reward, done, _ from env.step(action)
The clone's example creates MultitaskKitchenDomain with the OSC_POSITION controller, calls env.reset() and steps a four-element action
The clone also defines KitchenEnv in kitchen.py
The clone also defines MultitaskKitchenDomain in multitask_kitchen.py
The clone also defines ToolUseEnvBase in tool_use.py
The clone defines the hardest tool-use variant ToolUseEnv with its own cube and tool ranges
The package declares numpy, numba, scipy and mujoco-py as install dependencies; robosuite itself is installed separately

determinism.notes: the clone exposes no seed method and the robosuite reset takes no seed: the placement sampler draws the object pose from numpy's process-wide generator (hammer_place.py:443-456), so the MHS seed is recorded for the receipt only and does not select a state.  The package's fake is deterministic from its own fixed placeholder start state but is not the upstream environment

gaps: the fake backend is a physics-free stand-in: it keeps a placeholder end-effector position and a tick count, moves it by a placeholder gain, and integrates no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, actuators, sensors, cameras or noise; the upstream environment builds a robosuite/MuJoCo world

the observation is a placeholder dictionary with the robot keys the clone's get_state_vector names (hammer_place.py:530-533) and the activated robot0_joint_pos observable (hammer_place.py:332); the real observation also carries the object observations, robot0_contact, robot0_eef_force_norm and the agentview and robot0_eye_in_hand camera images that the constructor enables by default (hammer_place.py:28 and :43-45), and its array lengths depend on the robot and camera configuration. NOT COVERED: the camera image arrays
the fake reports reward 0.0 and done false and never reaches the cabinet success predicate (hammer_place.py:463-475): the task success, reward scaling and placement sampling are not modelled

there is no fixed timestep in the clone: control_freq is a constructor option with default 20 (hammer_place.py:39) and the physics step comes from the robosuite model, so timestep_ms is 0 and ticks count control steps, not physics steps

the action vector's shape is a constructor option: the documented benchmark action space is OSC_POSITION (3) plus Gripper (1) (environments.md:39) and the clone special-cases action_dim 4 (hammer_place.py:489-492), but controller_configs can select another controller, so the driver declares no action bound and accepts any non-empty numeric vector
the clone exposes no seed method and the reset takes no seed, so cap.world.reset.v1 records the seed without passing it to the environment; determinism.kind is none
the clone's step replaces done with _check_success and the returned info only adds history_ft and recent_ft (hammer_place.py:495-499), so a horizon timeout is not reported and truncated is false
only the first card entry symbol, HammerPlaceEnv, is served; the other four declared classes are other single-arm tasks and are not this driver
snapshot and restore are not offered by this package
robosuite, mujoco-py, numpy, numba and scipy were not installed and the upstream environment was never run, so no trajectory or observation of this package was compared with it
no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: the e-stop closes the environment and no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch and resets the environment; the last observation and tick stay readable
